channel.title: Latest alerts from washingtonpost.com
channel.description: An unofficial feed created by Derek Willis.

item.title: We got a sneak peek at fall’s best movies. Here are 8 worth seeing.
item.description: Our favorite films out of the Toronto International Film Festival were energetic, heartfelt and often gut-wrenchingly funny.

item.title: Trump pledges to open new Arctic military bases as he signs Greenland security deal
item.description: The agreement grants the United States wide-ranging powers to secure and defend the Arctic island as it remains Danish territory. The signing ceremony, which took place on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly, follows months of tension between Washington and its European allies over Greenland, with fears that a U.S. move to seize the territory by force could irreparably split the NATO alliance.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: Nope, late mother’s necklace does not go with that dress
item.description: Carolyn Hax: Nope, late mother’s necklace does not go with that dress

item.title: Trump warns United Nations he might ‘annihilate’ Iran if its leaders do not make a deal
item.description: President Donald Trump’s threat was a stark statement in a forum often focused on peace. In his remarks, he also repeated his claim that a peace deal would be likely after the midterm elections in November.

item.title: Man held in ICE facility after officer shot him is hospitalized after partial paralysis, lawyer says
item.description: The Venezuelan man had been transferred from a local hospital to a federal detention facility four hours after he was shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer in Austin on Sunday, despite having a bullet still lodged in his back, according to his attorney. He was taken to a hospital late Monday after experiencing paralysis on the left side of his body, the lawyer said.

item.title: Trump officials set to remove hundreds of thousands of Affordable Care Act enrollees, claiming widespread fraud
item.description: Vice President JD Vance’s anti-fraud task force is expected to say that the people were wrongly signed up for the government health care program. The administration also is set to suspend some brokers found to have wrongly signed up people for ACA coverage, according to people with knowledge of the announcement.

item.title: I attended an anti-vaccine conference. The joke ended quickly.
item.description: I am firmly pro-vaccine. Ridiculing those who are not helps no one.

item.title: Should you get a covid vaccine this fall? Here’s what to know.
item.description: In late August, the Food and Drug Administration approved updated covid-19 vaccine formulations that target the variants currently circulating around the country. But there hasn’t been new federal guidance this year on who should get the vaccine.

item.title: Media ban. GOP presidential race. Trump arch. Deportee database. Covid shots. Hungry bears. Fall movies. Catch up now.
item.description: Catch up in minutes.

item.title: ICE erasing immigrants with final deportation orders from its detainee locator database
item.description: The policy change, which took effect Sept. 15, leaves families and attorneys in the dark as they try to find out where someone has been taken. The new policy also bars immigration officers from sharing information about a detainee’s location with their attorneys or relatives by phone, according to two former Homeland Security officials briefed on the change.

item.title: Joe Manchin: What could make Congress wake up
item.description: Americans should consider voting independent in November. Here’s why, the former senator writes.

item.title: George Lucas’s colossal pet project could mark the end of the art museum as we know it, writes columnist Philip Kennicott
item.description: The Star Wars creator’s museum of “narrative art” in Los Angeles, which opens Tuesday, scrambles all the old categories and ideals.

item.title: Quarterback Jayden Daniels is injured again. Where do the Commanders go from here?
item.description: With Daniels sidelined for the foreseeable future, Washington’s defense is under increased pressure to step up.

item.title: Paramount settles with states over Warner Bros. Discovery merger, paving the way for a blockbuster unification
item.description: The decision is the latest twist in Paramount Skydance’s pursuit of Warner Bros. Discovery, a deal that would make the conglomerate one of the largest and most powerful companies in the entertainment business.

item.title: Is this how the world ends? Extinction scenarios are taking over the AI debate.
item.description: Thought experiments once deployed to sway AI insiders are now shaping the public imagination, circulating through Washington and influencing how lawmakers plan to govern a multitrillion-dollar industry. But some AI and policy experts wonder whether the parables could lead decision-makers astray.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: Teens’ dad marks passage of time by not missing a chance to lecture
item.description: Carolyn Hax: Teens’ dad marks passage of time by not missing a chance to lecture

item.title: He spent 11 months inside DOGE. Now he wants to set the record straight.
item.description: For many Americans, Elon Musk’s secretive cost-cutting project was a callous showcase of bending government to a billionaire’s will. For Tyler Hassen, it was an exhilarating, chaotic and sometimes scary experience — and one he would gladly live through again, he told The Washington Post in his first major interview detailing his forthcoming memoir, “Inside DOGE: The Real Story from a Senior Insider.”

item.title: A $1.2 trillion state allowance is stunting America’s growth
item.description: The U.S. government has become states’ piggy bank.

item.title: Major TV networks to halt shared video coverage of Trump over CNN ban
item.description: According to a memo obtained by The Washington Post, major television networks will halt pool coverage of the president in response to the White House’s ban of CNN, which was barred alongside MS NOW and Politico in recent days.

item.title: Inside Trump’s secret deals paying foreign governments to take unwanted deportees
item.description: The U.S. has pledged at least $410 million to expel migrants to at least 31 countries where they have no previous connection, internal records show.

item.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico to sue after Trump bans outlets from White House
item.description: The suit, expected to be filed Monday, alleges violations of the news organizations’ First Amendment free press rights and Fifth Amendment due process rights.

item.description: Catch up in minutes.

item.title: A melanoma vaccine was hailed as a breakthrough. Which cancers are next?
item.description: The reported success of an experimental drug that uses messenger RNA to deliver personalized skin cancer vaccines could herald a wave of new treatments that harness the potent technology for a range of cancers, researchers say.

item.title: ICE agent shoots, wounds man in Austin, city officials say
item.description: The man is in “stable but serious condition” after being shot in the torso, and was transported to a local trauma center, an Austin official said.

item.title: Scientists heard a knock at the door. It was a pelican in need of help.
item.description: A recent quiet morning at a Florida marine research facility was interrupted by the tapping of an injured bird. To a researcher’s shock, the animal seemed to have arrived at the facility on its own.

item.title: There’s a world war raging. You might be standing on the front lines.
item.description: Argentine ants have been fighting a global war for decades — and the logic looks uncannily human, Mark W. Moffett writes.

item.title: Russia recruited Ukrainian children to carry out attacks. They got caught.
item.description: Across Ukraine, at least 13 minors are imprisoned after being paid by Russia to strike at their own country.

item.title: The 13-year-old girl traversing the globe as a pro pickleball player
item.description: Trades! Visas! Middle school! There’s no rest for pickleball sensation Elsie Hendershot.

item.title: 3 science-backed home remedies to ease the common cold
item.description: Rest and hydration are essential, but these other strategies recommended by experts may also bring relief.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: Wife has tall orders for the spouse who does all the cooking
item.description: Carolyn Hax: Wife has tall orders for the spouse who does all the cooking

item.title: Trump and sons invest heavily in the AI economy as he resists calls for a slowdown of development
item.description: The Trump family’s expanding web of investments illustrates how the president’s personal wealth and his family’s increasingly technology-focused ventures overlap with one of the most consequential policy debates confronting his administration: how aggressively the government should respond to rapid advances in artificial intelligence.

item.title: She cheered a teen protest against ICE. Police charged her with a crime.
item.description: A local political feud over a high school protest became a brief national fixation when police charged a woman with contributing to the delinquency of a minor.

item.title: Trump says planned 250-foot arch will be a ‘military complex’ for drones and snipers
item.description: The president's new social media post about the triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery, which comes as veterans groups, historic preservationists and others attempt to stop the project, resembles his arguments for the need to build a ballroom at the White House.

item.title: How the surging cost of going out is changing American life
item.description: With the cost of concerts, sports games and restaurants far outpacing inflation, more people are staying home.

item.title: For 11 days, a lost hiker shouted for help. Then two kayakers appeared.
item.description: Craig Berg’s phone vanished in a swamp. As he sought help, he survived on freeze-dried food and “the most disgusting water that you could imagine.”

item.title: Diverse Texas campus bonds in anger after candidate’s racist post
item.description: At the University of Texas, Republican Bo French drew widespread, bipartisan condemnation for his attack on South Asian students celebrating their football team’s win.

item.title: Trump says he will form ‘AI Force’ and tap official responsible for the technology, but rejects calls for constraints
item.description: Some lawmakers and industry leaders have called for moving more slowly on the technology.

item.title: White House budget chief pushes for scrutiny of NIH grants in Oval Office clash
item.description: Russell Vought argued the agency has been funding “woke” priorities and suggested the president create a commission to review grants from the National Institutes of Health.

item.title: At this show, the acrobats are amazing. And they're cats.
item.description: The Amazing Acro-Cats, on tour through December, are coming to a litter box near you.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: Does she have to share pregnancy experience with her cheating ex?
item.description: She plans to co-parent with her ex. He wants to be involved with her pregnancy, too, and asked to “come over and rub my belly.”

item.title: Behind Trump’s public confidence, his private view of midterms is sobering
item.description: The president has been hearing blunt news from advisers about the GOP’s chances in the midterm elections and has signaled he understands that he has contributed to the poor political environment.

item.title: I put a chatbot to work on my grandmother’s Bergen-Belsen mystery
item.description: Family lore said she wrote an article about her concentration camp experience soon after liberation, Daniella Greenbaum Davis writes.

item.title: CNN, MS NOW say journalists blocked from White House after Trump announces ban on three outlets
item.description: President Donald Trump said Friday he would block MS NOW, CNN and Politico from White House grounds. News outlets and press advocacy groups condemned the move and said it was a violation of the First Amendment.

item.title: Secret contracts reveal undisclosed terms in Trump’s drug-pricing deals
item.description: The Trump administration’s confidential deals with pharmaceutical companies to lower U.S. drug prices include inducements to raise drug prices overseas and promise protection from President Donald Trump’s tariffs, according to documents shared with The Washington Post.

item.title: Hundreds of Kennedy Center supporters rally outside the shuttered arts institution, chanting ‘Hands off!’
item.description: The vigil, which had been in the works for months, took on fresh urgency at the end of a week that saw the doors to the marble building locked shut, while President Donald Trump indicated the structure could be “ripped down” if his name isn’t added to the institution.

item.title: Fight intensifies in California over the fate of homes falling into the sea
item.description: Homeowners are building a costly rock wall to hold back the ocean, escalating a battle over private property and what to do about years-long beach erosion amid storm damage and higher tides.

item.title: Trump says U.S. will defend Greenland as part of ‘permanent’ security deal with Denmark
item.description: The agreement, which Danish officials said is not final, stops far short of Trump's often-stated goal of taking possession of the territory.

item.title: Fresh layoffs begin at Kennedy Center as closure continues
item.description: The cuts come as the center’s main building remains closed during a widening legal battle over President Donald Trump’s transformation of the national cultural institution.

item.title: The nativist provocateur who keeps pushing the Texas GOP further right
item.description: Republican leaders criticized a recent post by Bo French attacking South Asian UT students. But many in the party have felt compelled to embrace parts of his ideology.

item.title: Trump says he’s banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House for reporting ‘fake news’
item.description: The president has consistently feuded with news organizations and at times tried to ban them and their journalists from the White House.
